title_ar: من خصائص المصطفى صلى الله عليه وسلم
title_en: Some of the Distinguishing Features of the Chosen One, God Bless Him and Grant Him Peace
body_ar:
لا منة علينا لأحد -بعد الله- مثل ما لهذا النبي الكريم، إذ هدانا الله به إلى الصراط المستقيم، ووقانا من حر نار الجحيم، وقد خصه الله بخصائص عظيمة، ومناقب كبيرة، منها أنه صاحب المقام المحمود الذي يحمده عليه جميع الخلائق حتى الأنبياء.
الشفاعة في الآخرة:
قال الشيخ: كذا من الذي اصطفي به الشفاعة لأهل الموقف قد اصطفي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وشرف بعدة أمور عمن سواه، منها الشفاعة العظمى، وقد جاء فيها عدد من الأحاديث، منها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (أوتيت خمساً لم يعطهن نبي قبلي)، وفي الحديث الآخر: (وأوتيت ستاً لم يعطهن نبي قبلي)، فذكر منهن: أنه كان النبي يبعث إلى قومه خاصة وبعث إلى الناس عامة. وأنه جعلت له الأرض مسجداً وطهوراً، فأيما رجل أدركته الصلاة فليصل. وأنه أحلت له الغنائم ولم تكن مباحة لمن سبقه. ومنها الحوض المشهود الذي يرده الناس، فهو مختص به صلى الله عليه وسلم. ومنها الشفاعة الكبرى، فهي من خصائصه صلى الله عليه وسلم. فهذه بعض الميزات التي اختص الله بها رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ومن أعظمها الشفاعة...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* No one — after God — has laid upon us a favour like that of this noble Prophet, since by him God guided us to the straight path and shielded us from the heat of the fire of Hell. God singled him out with mighty distinguishing features and great merits, among them that he is the possessor of the praised station, for which all creatures will praise him, even the prophets.

## Intercession in the hereafter

The Sheikh said: *So too, among the things for which he was chosen, intercession for the people of the standing-place was chosen for him.*

The Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, was ennobled with a number of things above everyone else, among them the greatest intercession, concerning which a number of reports have come. Among them are his words, God bless him and grant him peace: "I have been given five things that no prophet before me was given"; and in the other report: "And I have been given six things that no prophet before me was given." Among those he mentioned: that a prophet used to be sent to his own people in particular, whereas he was sent to people at large; that the earth was made for him a place of prayer and a means of purification, so that whichever man is overtaken by the time of prayer, let him pray; and that the spoils of war were made lawful for him, whereas they had not been permissible for those before him. Among them is the Pool that is witnessed, to which people come down; it belongs to him alone, God bless him and grant him peace. And among them is the great intercession, which is one of his distinguishing features, God bless him and grant him peace. These, then, are some of the marks of distinction with which God singled out His Messenger, God bless him and grant him peace, and the greatest of them is the intercession …

flags.context: the record breaks off and the full text sits behind a download
options: render with an excerpt banner and link the .doc
flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off on an ellipsis exactly where the intercession — named as the greatest of the distinguishing features, and the subject of the section heading — is about to be treated. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/L-38.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.arabic: الفقرة الافتتاحية مقابل ما بعد العنوان الفرعي
flags.context: the synopsis paragraph against the transcribed opening of the lesson
options: mark the synopsis as the site's own and the remainder as the Sheikh's words
present the whole record as the Sheikh's words
flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.context: the formula introducing each quoted line of the versified creed being commented on
options: read it as the author of the versified base text, distinct from the lecturer
read it as Sheikh al-Dedew quoting his own verse
flags.note: Getting this referent wrong would misattribute a creedal formulation, so it is flagged on every record in which the formula appears. These lessons are a commentary on a versified creed (nazm): the transcriber introduces each base-text line with 'the Sheikh, may God preserve him, said', and the commentary follows. 'حفظه الله' is used of the living, which at first sight fits Sheikh al-Dedew himself. Three passages inside the run settle it otherwise. Record 719 has the speaker giving thanks for 'completing the commentary on the Sheikh's versification' and describing what 'the Sheikh' chose to leave undetailed — a commentator does not ordinarily speak of his own base text that way while expounding it. Record 716 describes the base text as a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil ibn Ishaq by 'one of the scholars'. Record 718 introduces the same quoted lines with 'the versifier said'. The reading adopted throughout this slice is therefore that 'the Sheikh' is the living author of the versified base text and the lecturer is his commentator. The author is nowhere named, and the identification should be confirmed by the Sheikh's office before publication, because the bracketed verse and the prose around it carry different attributions.

flags.arabic: منها قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (أوتيت خمساً لم يعطهن نبي قبلي)، وفي الحديث الآخر: (وأوتيت ستاً لم يعطهن نبي قبلي)
flags.context: the two reports cited in the transcribed portion
options: keep the citation exactly as given, with no collection and no grading
supply the collections in which the reports are found
flags.note: Style guide section 4. The Sheikh says only that 'a number of reports have come' concerning the greatest intercession and cites two of them by their opening words. He names no collection, no narrator and no grading, and the English adds none. Note that he himself draws attention to the variation between the two — five in one report, six in the other — and does not reconcile them; the English does not reconcile them either. A reviewer will recognise the reports; that is not a licence to annotate them here.

options: read a transcription error for المورود
flags.note: The usual epithet for the Prophet's Pool in this context is 'المورود', the Pool come down to — which is also what the relative clause immediately following says: 'to which people come down'. 'المشهود' is either a distinct epithet or a transcription slip that anticipates nothing else in the sentence. Rendered as served and not corrected, per style guide section 11; the alternative is recorded so that the Sheikh's office can decide.

flags.context: the same distinguishing feature, named twice in one paragraph
options: render each as served — 'the greatest intercession', then 'the great intercession'
harmonise both to one English term
flags.note: The source names what appears to be the same thing twice, first as 'العظمى' and later as 'الكبرى', and lists it twice among the distinguishing features with other items in between. This may be two names for one thing, or a transcription artefact of spoken delivery. The English keeps the two Arabic words distinct rather than harmonising them, so that the duplication stays visible to a reviewer.

flags.arabic: وأنه أحلت له الغنائم ولم تكن مباحة لمن سبقه
flags.context: the third item in the list of things given to him
options: the spoils of war were made lawful for him, whereas they had not been permissible for those before him
booty was made lawful to him and was not allowed to those before him
flags.note: Two ruling words in one clause and both are in the fixed table. 'أحلت' is the verb of 'حلال', rendered 'made lawful'; 'مباحة' is 'مباح', fixed as 'permissible'. They are not interchangeable and the English keeps them apart. Note that this is reported speech inside a hadith and not a ruling the Sheikh is issuing.

flags.context: in the quoted line of verse
options: the people gathered for the reckoning
flags.note: 'الموقف' is the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection, before the reckoning. 'Standing-place' is flat but keeps the noun; the alternatives explain it, which a translation of a line of verse should not do. The record's title in the source's own section listing is 'مواقف القيامة' in the next record of the run, using the plural of the same word.

translator_notes: One of a run of fifteen records, IDs 707-721, in the written-creed section, all uploaded on 9 and 10 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and the first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off on an ellipsis; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/L-* series, numbered L-26 to L-39 in the same order as the IDs. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lesson was delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.

The source's final line, 'تحميل المادة' ('download the material'), is the label of a download link in the page furniture, not part of the text. It is recorded as source_download_link and omitted from body_ar and body_en.

The base text being commented on is identified inside this run. Record 719 has the Sheikh speaking of 'completing the commentary on the Sheikh's versification', and of that versifier's rendering of Khalil's Jāmiʿ in some five hundred lines; record 716 describes the base text as a versification of the Mukhtaṣar of Khalil ibn Ishaq whose opening section is on creed; and record 718 introduces the same quoted lines with 'the versifier said'. Taken together these settle that 'the Sheikh, may God preserve him' in this run is the living author of the versified base text and not the lecturer. The author is never named.
The English breaks the transcribed portion into two paragraphs where the source runs on, so that the quoted line of verse is visibly separated from the commentary. No word has been added or removed.

The quoted line is rendered as prose in italics per style guide section 4, and no rhymed English has been attempted. Its wording as served, 'كذا من الذي اصطفي به الشفاعة لأهل الموقف قد اصطفي', is elliptical and the English is correspondingly tentative.
'المقام المحمود' is rendered 'the praised station', a Qur'anic term (Sūrat al-Isrāʾ 17:79) which the synopsis uses without citing it; no citation has been supplied.
